chapter: Trumpet styles and early New Orleans scene
title: Reading bands and violin players in New Orleans
summary: Punch names reading bands such as the Tuxedo and the Josephs, and violinists.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: Now, who had the outstanding reading bands here in New Orleans when you got here in 1919?
Well, Joseph, they tell me, did a lot of reading in the tuxedas.
I can't call his name, I couldn't call it for you. He's down there on, on, on, first of the living room, I got a barbershop. Oh yeah.
There's a, there's a, there's a, John Joseph was the name.
He's a bass player. Uh huh. There's Nelson Joseph and, uh, Kaiser was there.

Kaiser, played the clarinet, didn't he? Yeah. Oh yeah. And they had a tall fella in the band. He was a good resistance. He was a reader. I think he played violin, but I can't think of his name. Well, let's see. I don't think he was in no relation to them.
There's a guy named Robichaud, John Robichaud was a violin player. No, John Robichaud, no. A.J. P. Rohn, Peter Boccage. No, none of them.
Paul Dominguez. A brown skin fella. Paul Dominguez.
I can't think of any other more violin players offhand.
Well, he was one. He was a good one too, but he lived uptown. All them you talking about, they lived downtown, was it?
Uh huh, yeah. They had that.
I can't, but I'm going to get somebody to tell me that guy's name.
Yeah, well. Did they have many good violin players when you got here?
Well, all I know is EJ, and Peter Owen, and Roe Bishore, and that fella you just called, Bocard or something.
He plays trumpet now. Yeah, them fellas. Them the only violin players I know.
